_comment: Code-region adaptation cases, run by BOTH ports (IMPORT-63) — `tests/js/import-regions.test.js`
asserts that `ImportRegions.adapt` produces `adapted`, and `tests/test_ocr.py` renders a sheet
of `target`'s shape with the caption drawn inside `anchored` and asserts that OCR, handed
`adapted`, still reads it. Before this fixture the two halves were tested apart: the JS side
checked the geometry and the Python side was only ever given hand-written boxes, so nothing
covered an adapt()-widened region actually reaching the crop — which is the path a facility
mixing sheet templates takes on every read.
`anchored` is the re-anchored box BEFORE `ADAPT_MARGIN` grows it: where the marked block
physically lands on the target sheet, and so where the caption is drawn. `adapted` is that box
grown 10% a side, which is what OCR is actually sent. The gap between the two is the estimate
the picker now shows the operator rather than applying invisibly.
Every number is derived by hand from `_axis` + `_widen`, not captured from a run — a fixture
blessed from the implementation it checks would only ever restate it.

cases.name: a same-shaped sheet keeps the fractions it was marked with
cases.why: Same aspect means one template printed at two scales, where the title block scales with the sheet. Plain fractions are already exactly right and re-anchoring would move a correct box.
caption: LEVEL 3 PLAN

cases.name: a centred block is re-anchored and grown onto a portrait sheet
cases.why: Its midpoint sits inside CENTRE_BAND on both axes, so it keeps its centre and its physical size: 0.10*2448=244.8pt wide on a 612pt page is 0.40, 0.06*1584=95.04pt tall on a 792pt page is 0.12, then 10% a side.
caption: GROUND FLOOR PLAN

cases.name: a bottom-right title block too wide for the target page clamps to the axis
cases.why: 0.22*2448=538.56pt does not fit 612pt at its original 195.84pt right margin, so the horizontal start clamps to 0 rather than overflowing. Vertically it keeps its 47.52pt bottom margin (0.06 of 792pt) and its 142.56pt height (0.18).
caption: SECOND BASEMENT
